messages:
meera: Quick heads-up — I hit a small but scary repro on staging where eviction + lease handoff can lead to a stale read being returned after ownership switches. Putting the steps here so we can sync.
ryan: ugh, can you paste the repro steps?
meera: steps:
1) tenant A pins prefix P, gets lease epoch 101
2) node evicts P (evict path writes tombstone + evict_token)
3) before tombstone fully observable, lease for A expires and B wins the lease with epoch 102
4) B serves request using a cache entry that was in-flight during eviction and returns stale value
this only happens when the eviction write and the lease update are not observed in the same order by other nodes
ryan: hmm so ordering between lease-epoch publish and eviction visibility is the root cause
samir: is the in-flight entry coming from a stale local cache or from a replicated snapshot?
meera: local in-memory slab on node 3. It had a queued response; eviction removed residency but the response had already been scheduled to be sent. When B took the lease, it assumed eviction completed.
tess: can you share the minimal log snippet? that helped last time
meera: sure:
```
[2024-07-12T12:03:21Z] node3: serve prefix P -> using cached slot id=0x7f3
[2024-07-12T12:03:21Z] node3: evict write: evict_token={epoch:101,slot_seq:4832}
[2024-07-12T12:03:21Z] cluster: lease change -> prefix P owner=node5 epoch=102
[2024-07-12T12:03:21Z] node3: response sent -> value v_old
```
olivia: that makes sense. So the system assumes evict write is authoritative, but there's no handshake to prevent in-flight responses after ownership transfer.
ryan: two axes of fixes I see:
- make eviction->handoff atomic or at least linearizable: publish lease change only after we confirm eviction visibility cluster-wide (expensive)
- make handoff tolerant: when a new owner sees an evict_token with earlier epoch, refuse to serve unless you validate with origin (fast path: demote instead of fully evict)
samir: alternative: attach incarnation tag to every outbound response (lease_epoch + node_incarnation). New owner can reject responses with older incarnation and drop them on the floor.
tess: that avoids cross-node sync but requires callers to respect rejections. Where do we enforce "reject"? at RPC layer or inside coalescer? Probably inside serve pipeline before writeback.
meera: quick tradeoffs:
- atomic visibility (CAS across KV/lease service): correct but increases p99 and complicates offline private deployments.
- incarnation tag on responses: lower latency but adds subtle failure modes (lost responses vs correctness). Might break some clients expecting eventual consistency without explicit error handling.
- demote path: when eviction starts, mark entry demoted and stop scheduling new responses; let inflight finish but keep origin validation on handoff. Cheaper but requires a demote state machine and metrics.
olivia: I like demote + incarnation tag as a hybrid. Demote prevents new responses; incarnation tag lets new owner drop late responses if they show up.
ryan: agree. Also add a small window where new owner performs a quick validation call to the old node for any suspiciously-timed requests (only in low-latency regions). Fallback for cross-region.
samir: we should also add telemetry: evict_handoff_mismatch, late_response_incarnation_rejects, demote_count. Make them tagged by tenant and prefix so we can monitor hotspots.
meera: plan proposal:
- implement demote state for prefix: transitions Evicting -> Demoted -> Evicted. Demoted prevents scheduling new responses and requires outbound responses to include lease_epoch+node_id tag.
- on handoff, new owner rejects responses with older lease_epoch and increments late_response_incarnation_rejects.
- add a light validation call for handoff that is rate-limited and only used in first N seconds after ownership change if we see anomalies.
- add smoke e2e that fuzzes concurrent eviction + handoff and asserts no stale responses reach client.
- docs update + rollout gate via canary and metric thresholds.
eng-runtime-bot: created issue #RAL-431: implement demote state + incarnation tagging (assignee: @samir, priority: p1). Linking PR checklist template.
tess: couple of implementation notes:
- demote should be cheap: flip a bit in residency slab and set per-slot "no_new_send".
- outgoing envelope: `resp_meta={lease_epoch:101, node_incarnation:node3-20240712-1}`
- new owner check is just `if resp_meta.lease_epoch < current_epoch then reject` (also accept equal if node_incarnation matches or if signed allowlist)
ryan: tests: add unit for slot demote, integration injection to simulate network reorder, and a perf run to measure p99 change. We should aim for <1% p99 regression.
meera: I'll draft the RFC follow-up patch with diagrams and add the telemetry names. Samir/Tess can grab the implementation tasks.
olivia: thanks all — this has bug risk for multi-tenant fairness, good catch Meera :tada:
samir: I'll pick up the initial PR for the demote bit and add the envelope change. Will ping for review once I have the smoke e2e harness.
ryan: +1. Let's sync in tomorrow eng-runtime weekly to lock the rollout gate criteria.
meera: thanks everyone.
